skill.name: api-documentation-generator
skill.description: Generate developer-friendly API documentation from code, including endpoints, parameters, authentication, errors, examples, and usage guidance.
skill.summary: Turn API code into structured documentation for REST, GraphQL, and WebSocket interfaces.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Incomplete API references slow integration and increase support work. This skill turns API code into structured documentation with examples, errors, authentication, and usage guidance.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes routes, methods, parameters, request bodies, responses, authentication, and error patterns.
Creates structured endpoint documentation with required fields, validation rules, status codes, and headers.
Produces request examples for cURL, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python.
Documents REST, GraphQL, and WebSocket interfaces.
Drafts OpenAPI specifications, Postman collections, quick starts, and troubleshooting guidance.
Covers pagination, filtering, sorting, rate limits, versioning, and deprecation notices.
limitations: Accuracy depends on complete source code, schemas, annotations, and business rules.
Generated examples and specifications require testing against the target environment.
The skill cannot confirm undocumented runtime behavior or production configuration.
Human review is required for security, compliance, and public release decisions.

use_cases.title: Document a New Service
use_cases.description: Create a consistent reference for every route before an internal service launches.

use_cases.title: Publish Integration Guides
use_cases.description: Prepare endpoint details, authentication steps, examples, and troubleshooting notes for external consumers.

use_cases.title: Refresh Legacy Documentation
use_cases.description: Compare current implementation details with outdated references and draft corrected documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Document One Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Document this endpoint from the supplied route and schema. Include its purpose, authentication, parameters, request body, responses, errors, and one cURL example.

prompt_templates.title: Document a REST Resource
prompt_templates.prompt: Create documentation for all supplied REST routes. Group endpoints by resource and include validation rules, status codes, pagination, filtering, and tested example placeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Create an API Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a developer guide from this codebase. Include an introduction, authentication, quick start, endpoint reference, data models, errors, rate limits, and changelog outline.

prompt_templates.title: Draft OpenAPI and Review Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an OpenAPI specification from the supplied implementation. Identify ambiguous behavior, missing schemas, undocumented errors, security assumptions, and examples that require runtime verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a specification and perform a documentation gap review.

output_examples.input: A user creation route, request schema, authentication middleware, and service errors.
output_examples.output: A Create User reference covering Bearer authentication, validated fields, success details, common errors, and request examples.

output_examples.input: GraphQL user query definitions and resolver behavior.
output_examples.output: A User Query guide describing arguments, selected fields, nested results, error behavior, variables, and response structure.

output_examples.input: Authentication routes for login and token refresh.
output_examples.output: An authentication guide explaining token creation, Authorization headers, expiration, refresh behavior, and relevant failure responses.

best_practices: Provide route code, schemas, middleware, tests, and current business rules.
Verify every generated request and response example against a controlled environment.
Review documentation whenever endpoints, validation, authentication, or response contracts change.
anti_patterns: Do not publish generated specifications without checking implementation details.
Do not use real credentials, tokens, personal data, or production secrets in examples.
Do not omit error cases, authentication requirements, limits, or deprecation information.

faq.question: Which API styles are supported?
faq.answer: The skill provides guidance for REST, GraphQL, and WebSocket APIs.

faq.question: Can it create an OpenAPI specification?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft an OpenAPI specification from supplied routes and schemas, but the result requires validation.

faq.question: Does it generate request examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It can prepare examples for cURL, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and other requested languages.

faq.question: Can it verify examples against a live API?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides documentation guidance and examples, but runtime testing remains the user's responsibility.

faq.question: What source material produces the best result?
faq.answer: Provide routes, schemas, middleware, tests, error definitions, authentication rules, and existing documentation.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Remove secrets and personal data before sharing code. Use clear placeholders for credentials, tokens, and user records.
